## 🎉 What's New in v0.15.1

**A bug-fix release, headlined by setpoints that stop wandering between modes.**

This release syncs with the upstream project and brings across four fixes, plus one of our own.

---

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

### 🌡️ Your temperature stays with the mode you set it in

**Set a temperature while cooling, come back to cooling later, and it's still there.**

Previously a setpoint captured in one mode could resurface in the other. The saved temperature was not scoped to a mode, and two places preferred it over the mode's own configured value — so a thermostat in **cool** could fall back to the preset's **heat** setpoint and start cooling toward it.

It showed up two ways:

- **Turning a preset off after switching modes.** Set heat to 20, pick a preset of 18/26, switch to cool (correctly 26), then turn the preset off — and you'd land on 20 instead of the cool value.
- **Anything re-applying the preset already active** — a scheduler tick, a UI resend, or re-selecting the same preset. One reporter had been running a watchdog automation to work around it.

Both paths now resolve the setpoint through the current mode's own bound.

- Details: #641, #643 (upstream)

### 🌀 Fan speed control for fans that connect late

Fans from integrations that come online after Home Assistant starts (ESPHome, MQTT) were left without speed control until a restart. Capability detection now retries when the entity appears, and a fan speed you picked while it was still missing gets applied once it arrives.

- Details: #636, #638 (upstream)

### 🔥 `fan_on_with_heater` works when you also have a cooler

The option had no effect on heater + cooler systems, because the fan already belonged to the cooler. It's now honoured when you opt in, without the two fighting over the shared fan.

- Details: #637, #639 (upstream)

### ⚙️ Reconfigure changes actually take effect

Once you'd saved Options for a thermostat, that snapshot silently shadowed anything you later changed through **Reconfigure** — including the temperature sensor, which isn't even editable in Options. Reconfigure reported success while the old value kept being used.

Reconfigure now clears that stale snapshot. To go with it, the reconfigure wizard reads your *effective* configuration when it opens, so settings you made in the Options flow — presets, openings, advanced settings — are carried through the wizard instead of being replaced by older values.

- Details: #631, #634 (upstream)

### 🔧 Late-arriving AC keeps its fan and swing controls

A wrapped AC that was offline at startup gained fan and swing passthrough correctly again; a regression introduced while merging the two fan fixes above stopped the capability refresh from reaching the thermostat's state.

---

## 📊 By the Numbers

- **5 bug fixes** — mode setpoints, late fans, fan with heater, reconfigure, wrapped AC capabilities
- **1690 tests** — all passing
- **100% backward compatible** — no configuration changes needed

---

## 🔄 Migration Guide

**Drop-in replacement.** No configuration changes required.

One behavior worth knowing: **Reconfigure** now clears the saved Options snapshot, which is what makes reconfigured values take effect at all. The wizard pre-fills from your effective configuration, so walk through it to the end and your existing settings carry over.
